resources.string: First specify the rapid acting insulin label in left menu→Settings→Display→IOB on your phone. This setting will be sent to the watch along with the amounts.

Blocked

Left middle menu→Mirror→”Mirror sends amounts” is set to prevent entering amounts in this app, because they will be overridden by amounts received from the mirror connection.

If this app doesn\'t receive amounts from a mirror connection, unset this option.

This setting is also changed, on both watch and phone, with left menu→Watch→WearOS config→”Amounts entered on watch”.

Location permission

Devices running Android 6 to 11 need location permission to find Bluetooth devices. This scanning for Bluetooth devices is needed for Aidex X, Accu-Check SmartGuide, CareSens Air and Dexcom G7 and Sibionics sensors and to receive glucose measurement from finger-stick glucose meters via Bluetooth.

Scanning for Bluetooth devices happens regularly when connecting and reconnecting to Bluetooth devices, it doesn’t happen only one time.

On Android 10 and Android 11 also location background permission is needed to enable this scanning for devices when Juggluco is in the background.

To allow Android to connect to these Bluetooth devices in the background, you need to select “Allow all the time” when giving Juggluco location permission. “Using the app” means having the app in the foreground.

This location permission is only used for finding Bluetooth devices and not for anything else.

NEARBY DEVICES permission

Juggluco needs NEARBY DEVICES permission to receive glucose values via Bluetooth from Freestyle Libre 2 and 3 sensors. If Juggluco receives these glucose values from Juggluco running on another phone or watch, Juggluco doesn’t need this permission.

To watches, Juggluco connects via the companion app of that watch, so that Juggluco itself doesn’t need this permission to connect to watches.

Notifications

Unless Juggluco is used with Freestyle Libre 0 sensors, Juggluco must remain active in the background to receive a glucose reading every minute either directly from the sensor via Bluetooth or via a network connection. To prevent apps from being killed by Android, Android requires apps to display a notification so users know the application is present in the background. The text “To connect with sensor” or “To exchange data” describes why Juggluco has to stay active in the background.

Juggluco also uses the notification to display the current glucose value and a change direction arrow.
